description: This walk follows a section of the England Coast path from Kings Lynn to Hunstanton. It's a 17 mile hike, following the path north out of King's Lynn to the coast and the Lynn Channel. The route then passes RSPB Snettisham and Heacham before finishing at Hunstanton. Following this expansive stretch of the England Coast Path offers a unique transition from the historic, maritime atmosphere of King's Lynn to the open, wild beauty of the Norfolk shoreline. As you leave the town behind and shadow the Lynn Channel, the landscape opens out into a vast expanse of saltmarshes and mudflats that define the edge of The Wash. This area is a significant habitat for coastal wildlife; you are likely to see grey herons and egrets stalking the shallows, while birds of prey like marsh harriers often hunt over the nearby reedbeds. The sense of isolation and the scale of the North Norfolk skies make this long-distance trek a truly immersive experience for hikers seeking a sense of adventure away from the crowds.As the route reaches the seaside villages of Heacham and Hunstanton, the terrain becomes firmer and more predictable, following the well-maintained sea walls and promenades. This section is particularly famous for its unusual westward orientation, providing a rare opportunity to watch the sun set over the sea on the east coast of England. The final leg into Hunstanton is framed by the town's iconic striped cliffs, where layers of red and white chalk create a striking geological landmark. Finishing at this traditional Victorian resort provides a satisfying conclusion to the 17-mile journey, with plenty of opportunities to enjoy local hospitality after a day exploring one of the most ecologically diverse stretches of the Norfolk Coast.
